discovery: Discovery of spin-orbit torques: electrical switching of magnetization by in-plane currents through spin-orbit coupling
subfield: Condensed matter physics: spintronics and magnetism
motivation: Miron and Gambardella showed in 2010-2011 that an in-plane current in ultrathin ferromagnet/heavy-metal heterostructures exerts torques large enough to switch perpendicular magnetization. These torques come from spin-orbit coupling, through the spin Hall effect and interfacial Rashba physics, so no second ferromagnetic polarizer is needed. Buhrman and coworkers then established the spin Hall mechanism quantitatively, using spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance and giant spin Hall switching in tantalum and tungsten, and built three-terminal devices from it. Together these works opened a field. Spin-orbit torques have been confirmed in hundreds of laboratories across metals, oxides, topological insulators and antiferromagnets. They now drive domain walls and skyrmions, enable electrical switching of antiferromagnets, and underpin SOT-MRAM, which industry is developing for fast, low-energy memory. This is a fundamental discovery about how relativistic spin-orbit interaction converts charge currents into angular momentum transfer to magnetic order. It has been validated widely and has lasting technological impact.
